event.summary: Keep the shared pause ownership regressions when removing tmux tests
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 647f0227b7f5b6c5fe443b2d5f0c4a20de0d5513. TLDR: This change removes checks that one stalled or displaced viewer cannot silence another viewer. Those protections still apply to the new terminals, but their replacement stream tests bypass the connection and ownership machinery the removed tests checked. Details: assigned 00800-001.patch:65-208 deletes a_stall_detaches_only_its_own_attachment_not_the_connections_others and a_pause_from_a_client_that_lost_a_takeover_cannot_silence_the_winner. The latter deliberately collides channel IDs on different supervisor connections and barriers after the stale pause; the former holds two independent sessions on one connection. service/connection.rs:2219-2231 still routes PauseOutput by both channel and notify.same_channel, and grid_stream.rs:98-103 explicitly shares stall attachment machinery. Replacement grid_stream/tests.rs:118-144 creates its own watch channel and GridStreamParts directly, so tests at :485-507 and :778-796 do not exercise set_attachment_paused or session attachment-map teardown. The retained connection.rs:3502-3551 test checks apply_pause_transition directly, not the ownership lookup. Targeted searches at this commit found no remaining tests for the lost-client pause/channel-collision or cross-attachment stall isolation scenarios. SPEC.md:3038-3066 promises one owner per session, no viewer slowing an unattached session, and a bounded stall detach. Suggested fix: migrate these two backend-independent integration scenarios to host/grid attachments rather than delete them with the tmux recovery tests. Suggested bucket: other (regression-test coverage loss only); confidence: confirmed by source for the test gap. could-be-highest: no established security or loss-of-work defect; current ownership code contains both required checks. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: none; parent owns queue coverage. Caveats: no runtime tests or reproductions; this does not claim the current implementation actually misroutes a pause or over-detaches. The original lead also considered removed mixed legacy-session tests; those cover a backend removed in the following commit, unlike these shared ownership scenarios. Their disappearance is not evidence of an implementation failure.

event.summary: Retain the stale-owner pause regression on terminal hosts
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 647f0227b7f5b6c5fe443b2d5f0c4a20de0d5513. TLDR: The change removes the integration check that a displaced viewer cannot pause its replacement, even though new terminals still use the same ownership lookup. Details: removed parent-side test a_pause_from_a_client_that_lost_a_takeover_cannot_silence_the_winner starts at :1452 (assigned 00800-001.patch:153-208). It creates two supervisor connections with equal numeric channel IDs, takes the session over on the second, sends PauseOutput from the displaced first, barriers on that connection, then requires fresh echoed output on the replacement. Nothing in that scenario depends on tmux recovery. service/connection.rs:2219-2231 still requires both a.channel == channel and a.notify.same_channel(tx); deleting the latter check would now leave the removed scenario untested. The grid-stream tests create their own pause watch directly (grid_stream/tests.rs:118-144), bypassing connection identity, while connection.rs:3502-3551 tests only the transition and timeout anchor. Broad git grep for pause_output( at this revision found two surviving e2e callers, tab_lifecycle_edges.rs:614 and terminal_tabs.rs:1442; both pause a currently owned channel and do not create a cross-connection channel collision. Suggested fix: preserve this backend-independent integration test using the ordinary host/grid harness and grid text observation helpers. Contract: SPEC.md:3038-3066 limits ownership to one client and prevents a viewer from slowing a session it is not attached to. Suggested bucket: other; confidence: confirmed by source for the lost regression coverage. could-be-highest: no established security or loss-of-work defect; current implementation has both ownership checks. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: none; parent owns queue coverage. Caveats: no execution performed; no claim that the current implementation actually misroutes a pause. Original broader consequence: both ownership and cross-attachment stall isolation appeared untested after deletion. Narrowed after source inspection: tab_lifecycle_edges.rs:535-660 retains stall-detach isolation for an agent and sibling tab, and terminal_tabs.rs:1397-1472 retains paused-tab/agent stream isolation, so no separate stall-isolation coverage finding is retained. Mixed legacy-session tests remain removed at this intermediate revision, but their disappearance alone does not establish an implementation defect; legacy serving is removed in the next assigned commit.

event.summary: Stale-owner pause coverage lost at 647f022 is restored at f560058
event.detail: Reviewed deletion commit: 647f0227b7f5b6c5fe443b2d5f0c4a20de0d5513; later repair commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e; verified surviving at pinned tip 00de0b6c9cf206f1a7c9c5ad1c76b5b10eaf85db. TLDR: The initial deletion removes a useful regression check, but an equivalent host-terminal test restores it before the pinned tip. Original consequence preserved: losing the test would allow a regression in which a displaced connection pauses a replacement with the same numeric channel to go undetected; no such production defect was established. Exact sensitivity: deletion-revision service/connection.rs:2225-2230 and tip :1552-1557 select an attachment with `.find(|a| a.channel == channel && a.notify.same_channel(tx))`. Omitting `a.notify.same_channel(tx)` is a meaningful competing implementation: after takeover, the only current attachment under the session/terminal key belongs to the winner and still has channel 1, so the loser’s PauseOutput would set the winner’s pause watch. The channel-only comparison passes; the connection-identity comparison rejects it. This is separate from sibling stall isolation. Test evidence: `git log -S` identifies f560058 as the addition of core/tests/host_terminals.rs::a_pause_from_a_client_that_lost_a_takeover_cannot_silence_the_winner (:3654-3707 there; :3649-3702 at tip). GridPeer::connect creates separate duplex connections through actual handle_connection (:3248-3273 at tip); the test attaches loser and winner on channel 1, requires the loser’s TakenOver notice, and waits for winner catch-up. It then executes `loser.send(&ControlMsg::PauseOutput { channel: 1 }).await; loser.round_trip(2).await; test_host.output(b"after the losing pause\r\n");` (tip :3689-3691). Its wait requires that new text or a detach, followed by asserting no detach, so a paused winner cannot pass on pre-pause output. Processing witness verified through source, not just helper documentation: round_trip sends ListSessions and waits for its reply (tip :3365-3378); handle_connection reads successive frames in its loop and awaits handle_control (:347-359,582-583,709-718), whose PauseOutput arm awaits set_attachment_paused inline (handlers.rs:3016-3018) before the next ListSessions frame can dispatch. Thus a spawned ListSessions handler cannot produce its reply before that preceding pause has been handled. The old correct predicate alone did not refute a missing test; this later equivalent test does repair ongoing coverage. Suggested bucket: other; confidence: confirmed by source. could-be-highest: no established security or loss-of-work defect; regression-test coverage only. proposed_drop: propose dropping only the claim that stale-owner pause coverage is still missing at the pinned tip, based on the equivalent f560058 test and verified processing witness; do not erase the intermediate deletion or treat it as covered at 647f022. Parent has accepted no drop. possible_cover: later source test at the named revision, no excluded coverage search. Previous proposed narrowing preserved: retained sibling tests refute the broad claim that stall isolation is entirely untested, but never substitute for stale-owner PauseOutput authorization. No runtime execution or reproduction; all conclusions are source analysis. No unresolved premise remains for l1.

Also :2395-2396: "The tab strip and every tab lookup merge the two kinds: tmux tabs first, in window order, then host tabs by their tags' creation times"; :2409-2410: "A takeover displaces the previous client's attachments to every terminal of the session, tmux and host alike". Suggested fix at that revision: keep equivalent tests by seeding earlier-release tmux state directly and adopting it, instead of relying on the removed create switch.
